newsitem.title: USA: U.S. July cash crude grades fail to excite market.
newsitem.headline: U.S. July cash crude grades fail to excite market.

text.p: July cash crude grade barrels failed to excite a slumbering U.S. domestic market Tuesday morning, leaving differentials steady against a sharply lower benchmark price.
"We had a long weekend, and it's the normal first day of trading for a new month where nobody wants to trade," said a cash dealer in Houston.
June crude business faded from view following pipeline scheduling day on Friday.
July West Texas Intermediate/Cushing was talked nearly 80 cents lower at $20.80-90 a barrel, and held a seven cents discount to second month August WTI.

Outright prices were pressured by technical selling on the NYMEX futures market. Some traders said Iran's election of a new "moderate" prime minister this past weekend took some of the steam out of the market.

On the domestic grade front, Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James was talked at 10-3 cents under the July marker, with Midland/WTI around 35-30 cents under and Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire 55-45 cheaper than benchmark values.
Sour barrels also failed to move from Friday talk, or attract fresh deals.

Traders said the expected drumbeat ahead of mid-June's OPEC meeting and possible American roadblocks for renewal of the Iraq-U.N. oil-for-food accord, would bolster sour differentials in the near-term.
"West Texas Sour will probably get weaker before it gets stronger, but in the end, the talk from OPEC and Iraq will make us stronger," said a Texas cash broker.
July Postings Plus was quoted at steady prices around $1.90-$2.05.
